chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ibn Abi Hamza, who said:
I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about a man who has four wives, and he divorces one of them; does he marry another in her place? He said, 'No, until her waiting period (iddah) expires.'
ai.seo_question: Can a man with four wives marry a new wife immediately after divorcing one, or must he wait for the waiting period to end?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the concept of polygyny is refined to clarify that the limit of four wives applies to those currently in active marital bonds, not merely those recently divorced. Consequently, a man must wait for the 'iddah' (waiting period) of the divorced wife to conclude before contracting a new marriage, ensuring the count of four distinct, simultaneously married wives is maintained. This ruling underscores the precision in Shia jurisprudence regarding the temporal boundaries of marital status during the transition period of divorce.
